answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token for a cooling-off period before it may vote on reputation or claim rewards. The ledger caps each token’s influence, so splitting one stake across a hundred accounts adds no weight. A pearl, lantern, or onyx identity faces the same rule: to manufacture influence, an attacker must acquire and immobilize more capital, paying opportunity cost and risking slashing if the identities coordinate fraudulently.
